## Likely Causes for Your Sore Throat and Cold Symptoms
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

Your symptom pattern — **4 days of sore throat, low-grade fever, fatigue, dry cough, and runny nose** — most strongly fits a **viral upper respiratory infection** such as a common cold or mild flu-like illness. Allergies are possible for the runny nose and cough, but **fever and fatigue make infection more likely** than allergies alone.

## Symptom Pattern and What It Suggests
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cloud-sun.svg

- **Viral infection:** Most likely if symptoms include sore throat, cough, fever, body tiredness, and runny nose.
- **Allergies:** More likely if there is **itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, no fever**, and symptoms come and go with exposure.
- **Strep throat:** Less likely when cough and runny nose are present, because strep usually causes a **more sudden severe sore throat, fever, and no cough**.
- **COVID-19 or flu:** Also possible, especially if there was recent exposure, body aches, headache, or worsening fatigue.

## Home Care and Over-the-Counter Options
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

- **Rest and fluids:** Water, broth, tea, and electrolyte drinks can help.
- **Warm salt-water gargles:** 1/2 teaspoon salt in a cup of warm water, several times a day.
- **Honey:** Can soothe cough and throat irritation; avoid in children under 1 year, but fine for adults.
- **Throat lozenges or hard candies:** Helpful for throat comfort and dryness.
- **Acetaminophen or ibuprofen:** Can help with fever, throat pain, and aches if you normally tolerate them.
- **Saline nasal spray or rinse:** Useful for runny nose and post-nasal drip.
- **Humidifier or steam:** May reduce throat dryness and cough.

### OTC Choices to Consider
- **For fever/pain:** Acetaminophen or ibuprofen, following the package directions.
- **For runny nose:** A non-drowsy antihistamine may help if symptoms seem allergy-like.
- **For cough:** Honey, lozenges, or a cough suppressant if the cough is keeping you from resting.
- **For congestion/post-nasal drip:** Saline spray or rinse first; decongestants may help some adults but are not ideal for everyone.

Because you are **allergic to penicillin**, avoid penicillin-family antibiotics if a clinician ever prescribes treatment. Also, most sore throats like this **do not need antibiotics** unless a bacterial cause is confirmed.

## When Medical Attention Is Needed
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg

Seek medical care if you develop any of the following:
- **Trouble breathing**
- **Chest pain**
- **Severe trouble swallowing**
- **Drooling or inability to keep fluids down**
- **One-sided throat swelling**
- **A rash, especially with fever**
- **Fever that becomes high or lasts more than about 3 days**
- **Symptoms lasting more than 7–10 days without improvement**
- **Worsening instead of gradually improving**
- **Signs of dehydration** such as very dark urine, dizziness, or minimal urination

## Quick Actions
- **If you can, test for COVID-19** if exposure is possible or if you need to protect others.
- **Use supportive care for 24–48 hours** and watch whether symptoms start improving.
- **Contact a clinician sooner** if you have severe throat pain, high fever, or symptoms that worsen.

## Sources
- CDC — Common Cold: https://www.cdc.gov/common-cold/
- CDC — Strep Throat: https://www.cdc.gov/group-a-strep/about/strep-throat.html
- NHS — Sore throat: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/sore-throat/
